title: add benchmark-lab profiling baselines and reporting pipeline v82
author: Sofia Martinez
description: Motivation: We need a repeatable set of profiling baselines and a robust reporting pipeline to track regressions across recent runtime optimizations (adaptive batching, KV-cache reuse) and new quantization kernels. This PR introduces the v82 profiling baselines, a set of representative workload runners (cpu/gpu/multi-variant), and an updated reporting pipeline that aggregates per-run latency/cost/trace data into the benchmark dashboard. Summary of changes: - Add profiling baselines YAML (benchmark-lab/profiling/baselines_v82.yaml) capturing canonical sequences, token distributions, and reference latency/throughput numbers. - Add representative workload runners for mixed and multi-variant workloads (benchmark-lab/runners/representative_cpu_runner.py, representative_gpu_runner.py). Runners support prefix caching and configurable sequence-length distributions. - Update reporting pipeline (benchmark-lab/reporting/pipeline_v82.yaml) to ingest runner outputs, enrich with trace IDs, and push summarized metrics to the benchmark DB and Grafana dashboards. - CI workflow additions: ci/workflows/benchmark-lab.yml adds nightly execution and a lightweight PR smoke check. - Utilities: scripts/collect_metrics.py and scripts/normalize_profiles.py to standardize runner outputs. - Docs: docs/benchmark-lab/README.md updated with runner config and how to reproduce baselines. Checklist: [x] Baselines defined and verified against current main runtime [x] Runners exercise prefix caching and batching knobs [x] Reporting pipeline tested end-to-end on staging S3 and test DB [x] CI smoke job added to prevent regressions on PRs [x] Release notes drafted How tested: - Local runs against dockerized runtime to validate measurements and KV cache behavior. - End-to-end run on staging cluster (3 runs across different instance types) to validate pipeline ingestion, normalization, and dashboarding. - CI smoke job executes a single short-run as part of the PR to catch regressions. Observed transient test flake on first CI run (timing-sensitive), re-ran and consolidated tolerances. Rollout plan: Merge to main; nightly job will produce v82 baselines and report to the benchmark dashboard. Alerting will be enabled for >10% regression in p95 latency or >15% regression in cost/token compared to baselines. Backward compatibility: New runners are additive; the reporting pipeline is backward compatible with older baseline schema (fallback for schema v80/v81 present). No breaking changes to consumers. Release notes: Adds benchmark-lab profiling baselines (v82), representative workload runners (cpu/gpu/multi-variant), and a stable reporting pipeline to collect and surface profiling metrics to dashboards and alerts.
